Verdict: ACCEPT under the following explicitly stated dependenciesThe new  $37/39$  theorem is mathematically sound on the stated complete-source domain. I found no counterconfiguration in the arbitrary-dimensional Y/X geometry, the shared defect-pool allocation, the negative-long-leg injection, or the final coefficient arithmetic.The acceptance is conditional on the following established facts, which are the exact dependencies used by the proof:Complete occupied-gate catalogue.Every occupied gate has the stated phase-01, phase-10, or phase-11 form for arbitrary legal even dimensions; phase-10 activation is valid for arbitrary incoming dimensions; the longitudinal and transverse coordinate charts in Section 1 are complete.Original support and endpoint semantics.Unactivated positive terminals retain their beyond-tip supports; anchors and retained supports have the stated final degree behavior; consumed supports remain occupied final endpoints; original endpoint ownership is not reassigned.Previous  $C^\ast$  compensation theorem.Blank-gate witnesses, old occupied-gate forced-corner witnesses, their source-labelled injectivity, and their cross-type nonreuse are valid for all prior  $C^\ast$  dimensions.Short-leg defect injection.The hypotheses used for the  $Y$ -witness tile  $Q$ —the negative pair profile, endpoint degrees, the protected positive endpoint, the finally blank corner, and absence of positive support in  $Q$ —are available in the global form of SHORT_LEG_DEFECT_INJECTION.md, Sections 3–4, for all relevant orientations and dimensions.Global canonical donor-tile injection in the strong form used in Section 5.For every actual marked canonical side of a special  $X$ , the relevant occupied gate endpoint lies in the same physical donor tile assigned to that source/side label, even if the old marked-side witness is a different endpoint and the consumed support is different again. Distinct source/side labels have distinct physical donor tiles.Terminal-to-leg uniqueness.A gate endpoint identified as an original terminal belongs to one immutable negative  $U$ , and to one source-labelled original leg occurrence. Two distinct such terminal endpoints may belong to the same negative  $U$ , but then they are its two distinct leg occurrences.Marked-side and matching budgets. $G\le4B$ , where  $B$  is the number of negative  $U$ -sources, and original matching edges are partitioned and counted once.Representative ledger.  
$$\sigma\ge\mu=N+R-G,\qquad R\ge0,\qquad
2R=A+U_0+Z_0+H,$$
together with the unchanged positive/negative matching partition.The note itself states the strong same-donor-tile clause in Section 5. If the prior donor-tile theorem established only injectivity of the old assigned mark witnesses, without establishing that the special gate endpoint lies in the same physical donor tile, then that would be a real gap. Under the strong clause explicitly used in the note, the injection is valid.1. Arbitrary-dimensional Y geometryAll coordinates below are read as (row, column).For the normalized  $U(8,6,8)$ , unactivated terminals force
$$(7,2)\quad\text{and}\quad(9,7)$$
to be finally blank.Left gateA phase-01 corner is excluded in both orientations:if its downward near leg has height  $h\ge6$ , it contains  $(7,2)$  as an endpoint;if  $h=4$ , the same point is the beyond-tip support;the other phase-01 orientation has a downward bar of breadth at least six and contains  $(7,2)$  as an endpoint.A longitudinal phase-11 owner has near stem column  $2$ , rows  $2,\ldots,h+2$ . Avoiding  $(7,2)$  gives
$$h+2<7.$$
Since  $h\ge4$  is even,
$$h=4.$$
Its bar is rows  $5,6$ , columns  $2,\ldots,v+1$ . The positive producer owns  $(5,8)$ , so
$$v+1<8.$$
With  $v\ge6$  even, this forces
$$v=6.$$
The far stem is column  $7$ , rows  $6-e,\ldots,6$ . If  $e\ge6$ , it contains  $(1,7)$ , which belongs to the producer’s original bar. Therefore
$$e=4.$$
Thus the longitudinal owner is exactly the inverted  $U(6,4,4)$ , with chart
$$(r,c)\mapsto(6-r,c+1).$$
Its far stem contains  $(2,7)$ , so this same source owns both canonical gates.Excluding a transverse left ownerFor a transverse phase-11 left owner, the near stem lies in row  $2$ , columns  $2,\ldots,h+2$ . Avoiding the producer’s  $(2,8)$  gives  $h=4$ . The bar then occupies columns  $5,6$ , rows  $2,\ldots,v+1$ , so it does not own  $(2,7)$ .At the right gate:every phase-01 corner and every transverse phase-11 owner reaches  $(2,6)$ , already occupied by the left transverse owner;a right longitudinal owner avoiding  $(9,7)$  has incident height  $k\in\{4,6\}$ ;its bar contains  $(k+1,6)$ , namely  $(5,6)$  or  $(7,6)$ , both inside the left bar.Thus the transverse case is impossible. The inverted  $U(6,4,4)$  is forced.The Y witness tileLet
$$Q=\{6,7\}\times\{2,3\},$$
meaning rows  $6,7$  and columns  $2,3$ .The forced owner has the original pair
$$\{(6,2),(6,3)\}$$
in  $Q$ , with no original support in  $Q$ . The point  $(7,2)$  is finally blank.The remaining point  $(7,3)$  cannot be a retained support. It already has the occupied neighbor  $(6,3)$ ; its own original anchor would create a second occupied neighbor unless that anchor were  $(6,3)$ . In that exceptional case endpoint disjointness identifies its source with the pair owner, but the pair owner has no original support at  $(7,3)$ .Therefore  $Q$  is either:an  $L2_{\mathrm{bar}}$  defect containing only the pair; oran  $L3$  defect containing the pair plus one singleton.In either case it contributes at least one actual  $H$ -unit.The proof does not claim two units. The other symmetric outside corner need not be nonfull, and the note correctly uses only one witness for  $Y$ . Reflection handles  $U(8,8,6)$ .2. Arbitrary-dimensional X geometryFor  $X=U(8,4,10)$ , unactivated terminals force
$$(5,2)\quad\text{and}\quad(11,7)$$
to be finally blank.At the left gate:both phase-01 orientations contain  $(5,2)$ ;every longitudinal phase-11 owner contains  $(5,2)$ .Thus the left owner is transverse phase-11. Avoiding the producer’s  $(2,8)$  forces its incident height to be  $4$ , and its bar occupies columns  $5,6$ , rows  $2,\ldots,v+1$ .At the right gate:phase-01 and transverse phase-11 owners collide at  $(2,6)$ ;a right longitudinal owner avoiding  $(11,7)$  has  $k\in\{4,6,8\}$ ; $k=4$  and  $k=6$  collide with the left bar at  $(5,6)$  and  $(7,6)$ ;hence  $k=8$ .The right bar then contains  $(9,6)$ . If the left breadth were  $v\ge8$ , the left bar would also contain  $(9,6)$ . Therefore
$$v=6.$$
The right gate  $(2,7)$  is consequently an original terminal of a negative phase-11  $U$  with incident leg length  $8$ . No restriction on that negative source’s breadth or other leg is needed. Reflection gives the  $U(8,10,4)$  case.The geometry is therefore genuinely all-parameter. The finite role masks are only corroboration.3. The shared compensation pool is correctly assembledFor the  $C^\ast$  doubles:a one-activation source contributes one source-labelled  $A$ -occurrence;a two-activation source contributes two;a zero-activation source with a blank gate contributes two slots from one blank canonical tile;a zero-activation source with both gates occupied contributes the two old forced-corner witnesses.The new  $U(8,4,8)$  and  $U(8,8,4)$  cases cannot have both gates occupied, so they fall into the blank-gate branch already accepted in the  $35/37$  theorem.For each cost-14 source that is not special, the three branches are exhaustive:it has an activation;it has no activation but has a blank gate;it has no activation and no blank gate, in which case it is  $Y$  or its reflection.Thus exactly  $p-x$  cost-14 sources contribute one additional resource unit.Nonreuse of Y witnessesThe  $Y$ -witness tile  $Q$  cannot be the forced witness of another  $Y$  source or of an old  $C^\ast$  forced witness.The reason is the accepted short-leg reconstruction:a nonfull tile cannot contain two endpoint-disjoint original pair profiles;the pair-owner endpoint degrees distinguish the two pair corners;the complete  $U$  fixes the bar direction;the pair corner and bar direction reconstruct the external positive endpoint;two distinct positive sources using  $Q$  would therefore share that external endpoint and violate original endpoint disjointness.This applies across the old forced-witness pool and the new  $Y$ -witness pool.Nonreuse with blank canonical tilesThe eight canonical donor orientations are also exhausted:selected corner  $(1,0)$  is the finally blank point;selected corner  $(0,1)$  has an anchor that is an endpoint of the negative pair owner;selected corner  $(0,0)$  has either a negative endpoint anchor or the protected positive endpoint;selected corner  $(1,1)$  either has an occupied gate or the protected positive endpoint.Thus  $Q$  cannot be any blank canonical donor tile. This is the needed cross-type exclusion, not merely a same-type forced-witness argument.Consequently all selected resources are distinct within the relevant identity class, and  $A$ -occurrences and  $H$ -slots remain separate even if their coordinates coincide. The exact identity gives
$$2R\ge2z+s+2t+p-x.$$
No  $U_0$ ,  $Z_0$ , full-tile credit, source charge, or additional area term is spent.4. The negative-long-leg injection is valid with the stated donor-tile dependencyFor a special  $X$ , the height-ten side has a right occupied gate. The geometric argument identifies that gate point as an original terminal of a negative phase-11  $U$  whose incident leg has length  $8$ .The important distinctions are handled correctly:the gate endpoint is not required to be the endpoint used by the old marked-side assignment;the gate endpoint is not the consumed support that characterized the mark;the gate endpoint is instead used as an original terminal in its own right;the same physical donor-tile clause puts that endpoint in the physical tile assigned to the special source/side label.With the strong donor-tile dependency:distinct special source/side labels give distinct physical donor tiles;the chosen gate endpoints are distinct;each gate endpoint is a terminal of one immutable negative  $U$ ;each terminal determines one source-labelled original leg occurrence.If two special sources map to the same negative  $U$ , they must map to its two distinct terminal/leg occurrences. They cannot map twice to the same leg occurrence.Let  $L$  be the total number of negative original legs of length at least  $8$ , and  $B$  the number of negative  $U$ -sources. Then  $L\ge x$ .For a negative  $U(v,h,e)$ , if  $b$  of its legs have length at least  $8$ , then
$$h+e\ge8+4b$$
and therefore
$$m=v+\frac{h+e}{2}-1
\ge6+\frac{8+4b}{2}-1
=9+2b.$$
Summing each negative source once gives
$$M_{\mathrm{minus}}\ge9B+2L\ge9B+2x.$$
The independent marked-side budget gives
$$G\le4B.$$
Therefore
$$4M_{\mathrm{minus}}
\ge36B+8L
\ge9G+8x.$$
This does not count a negative source’s matching twice. If one negative  $U$  receives two special injections on its two legs, the single matching size of that source is bounded by  $9+4$ , exactly accounting for both increments.The only dependency that must be made explicit in the project’s canonical donor-tile theorem is the same-tile gate-endpoint clause. Distinctness of the old assigned mark witnesses alone would not suffice. The present note states that stronger clause, so the written argument is valid under it.5. Matching-size partitionThe cost-14 list is complete outside  $C^\ast$ :
$$U(8,6,8),\quad U(8,8,6),\quad
U(8,4,10),\quad U(8,10,4).$$
Other cost-14 shapes, such as  $U(10,4,6)$ , already lie in  $C^\ast$ . Every remaining actual double counted by  $q$  has matching size at least  $15$ .Thus the positive matching contribution is
$$M_+\ge9N+5p+6q.$$
The positive and negative original matching partitions are disjoint, so each original matching edge is counted once. Combining with the long-leg budget gives
$$4|M|
\ge36N+20p+24q+9G+8x.$$
This is a size estimate, not a second use of the defect pool.6. Final coefficient arithmeticLet  $n_1$  denote one-mark positives. The exact source census is
$$N=n_0+n_1+z+s+t+p+q,$$

$$G=n_1+2(z+s+t+p+q),$$
and therefore
$$\mu=n_0+R-z-s-t-p-q.$$
From the reserve inequality,
$$2R\ge2z+s+2t+p-x.$$
If  $\mu=-\ell<0$ , then  $n_0\ge0$  gives
$$2\ell\le2q+s+p+x.$$
Also,
$$N\ge s+p+q,\qquad R\ge0.$$
Substituting  $G=N+R+\ell$  into the matching bound gives
$$\begin{aligned}
4|M|
&\ge45N+20p+24q+9R+9\ell+8x\\
&\ge45s+65p+69q+9\ell+8x.
\end{aligned}$$
Now put
$$C=45s+65p+69q+8x,
\qquad
D=2q+s+p+x.$$
The displayed difference is
$$2C-69D=21s+61p-53x.$$
Since  $0\le x\le p$ ,
$$21s+61p-53x
\ge21s+8p
\ge0.$$
Hence
$$C\ge\frac{69}{2}D\ge69\ell.$$
Therefore
$$4|M|\ge69\ell+9\ell=78\ell.$$
So
$$\ell\le\frac{2|M|}{39},
\qquad
\sigma\ge\mu\ge-\frac{2|M|}{39}.$$
Using
$$\sigma=\frac{mn}{2}-|T_{\mathrm{sel}}|-|M|,$$
we obtain
$$|T_{\mathrm{sel}}|+\frac{37}{39}|M|
\le\frac{mn}{2}.$$
Equivalently,
$$78|T_{\mathrm{sel}}|+74|M|\le39mn.$$
For  $\mu\ge0$ , the ledger gives  $\sigma\ge0$ , so coefficient one holds for that individual configuration.The coefficient comparisons are also correct:
$$\frac{37}{39}-\frac{35}{37}
=\frac{4}{1443},$$
and
$$\frac{37}{39}-\frac56
=\frac{3}{26}.$$
As stated, the numerical improvement is strict when  $|M|>0$ .7. Lean scopeThe supplied Lean statements match the written arithmetic:negative_long_leg_size proves the  $9+2b$  source-size bound;negative_mark_and_long_leg_budget combines marked-side capacity with long-leg surplus;conditional_shared_reserve_margin proves the reserve inequality in the required signed form;conditional_matching_budget proves the combined positive/negative matching budget;conditional_scaled_margin proves the  $39$ -scaled slack inequality;conditional_coefficient converts that inequality into
$$78|T_{\mathrm{sel}}|+74|M|\le39mn.$$
These Lean statements do not prove the source-role adapters, same-tile gate-endpoint bridge, forced-pair ownership, global physical injection, or arbitrary-source ledger. The note correctly identifies those as written dependencies. The absence of complete new Y/X fixtures is therefore not a defect, because the universal proof is not being inferred from finite fixture coverage.The remaining allocation patterns may still fail, and a failed candidate allocation is not a counterexample to the target inequality. The theorem only needs the matching-cost bound and the shared reserve inequality; it does not assert arbitrary-grid coverage, geometric sharpness, coefficient one, or realization of the remaining connected patterns.Final decision: ACCEPT under the enumerated dependencies above.
